title: translations.json — the written form
description: The file a Core writes beside a game and the site publishes. This is the WRITTEN form: what a current Core must produce, and what the site takes at upload without tolerance. Readers are more lenient (see cases.json, `read`), the site's door slightly more so (`upload`). The names under `properties` are metadata, and no other: every other key is a line of the game's text, in the source language, translated by the value — including a text that begins with an underscore (a signature line drawn with them, a label). One tolerance belongs to readers, not to this form: an underscore name a reader does not know, whose value is not shaped like a line, is a newer writer's metadata and is left alone (common TranslationFileKeys, corpus rules/translation_file_keys.json). Line endings are LF only, in keys and values AND in every text of the format 2 (written forms, the was / to / own of a link, a refused entry): every reader normalises CRLF then a lone CR to LF before anything else (common LineEndings, corpus rules/line_endings.json), and the hash is computed on the normalised form. A file from elsewhere that holds a CR in any of them is normalised, never refused; a writer of this library never produces one (LineWrites carriage-return-in-text).

_engine_version.description: The placeholder format the lines were written with. 1 = [!v*N] for numbers, [!t*N] for tags, [!STR*N] for variables, [!nl] for a line break. A reader migrates older forms; a Core writes the current one.

_uuid.description: The lineage. Generated once for a new file, kept through download, upload, contribution and update; replaced only by a fork. Every reader that finds none gives the file a fresh one.

_source_language.description: The game's language, as stated by the file. Absent until settled; never "auto" in the written form (a mode is not an answer — a reader hands "auto" over unjudged).

_target_language.description: The language the values are in. Absent until settled.

_local_changes.description: Lines changed since the last sync with the server, recounted against the ancestor at every write. A writer omits it at 0.

_metadata_dirty.description: The settings sections changed since the last sync. A writer omits it when false.

_game.description: Which game the file was written for, as the Core detected it.

name.description: The product name, or the game folder's name when there is none.

steam_id.description: The Steam app id as a string, or null for a game that has none. Never a number.

_source.description: Where the file stands against the server. Written only once the file has met it.

hash.description: The server's file_hash at the last sync (download or upload). Compared with the server's current hash to tell 'up to date' from 'update available'.

main_hash.description: For a branch: the Main's hash at the last merge from it.

site_id.description: The server row of this lineage's line for this account — the only handle an anonymous download keeps.

_forked_from.description: Present on a fork only: where it came from, frozen at the moment of the fork and never recomputed.

resolved_lines.description: How many translated lines were taken, a snapshot at the fork.

content_hash.description: The content taken, without the lineage — what says whether the fork is still the copy. Absent from a fork made before the key existed: 'we cannot tell'.

_fonts.description: Settings section `fonts`: an inventory keyed by font name. Internal shape: a later artefact.

_font_overrides.description: Settings section `font_rules`: ordered, first match wins. Internal shape: a later artefact.

_image_replacements.description: Settings section `images`. Internal shape: a later artefact.

_exclusions.description: Settings section `exclusions`: path patterns whose text is never sent. Internal shape: a later artefact.

_variables.description: Settings section `variables`: game values lifted out of texts as [!STR*N]. Internal shape: a later artefact.

_settings.description: Settings section `game_settings`: per-game switches. Internal shape: a later artefact.

_lists.description: Format 2 only. What the game's own lists hold, for the templates whose slots (`[!L*name]`) read them: imposed by the game, read by the extraction, edited by nobody — the most recent extraction replaces it, so it is never merged line by line. A slot of a line may name only a list found here (spec/translation-file `x-writer-guarantees`). NOT part of the content hash yet (open question, analyse/smart-suivi-socle.md). Anything else the extraction keeps (`field`, `row`, `witnesses`…) is provenance and diagnosis: internal shape, a later artefact.

lists.description: The lists, by name. A name holds none of ] [ : = * (see x-markers). A slot of a template is read on the text the game SHOWS: each slot takes the entry of its list that stands there, and nothing pairs the rows of two lists — a `row`, a `field` or any other key the extraction keeps beside `values` is provenance, tolerated and read by nobody.

values.description: The entries, in the game's own order.

join.description: How repeated entries are joined when no text holds them.

tokens.description: The game's own tokens (`#PlayerName#`, `{p3}`): literal texts its code replaces by a computed one before showing a text. Written by the extraction, each once, in the ordinal order of their texts (UTF-16 code units); read by the mod and by the Manager; with no translation; not `_variables`. Absent = none known. Never a pattern. See spec/translation-file/tokens.md.

x-hash-key-order.description: Every object key of the canonical document the content hash is taken of (the lines, and inside a line `forms`, `use`, `class`, `unlinked`) is sorted by UTF-16 CODE UNIT, as text — never as a number, never by culture, never by UTF-8 byte or code point: the order of C# StringComparer.Ordinal, which every published hash was computed with. It differs from the byte order as soon as a key starts beyond the Basic Multilingual Plane (units D800-DFFF) and another in U+E000-U+FFFF (full-width forms, private use): the first sorts BEFORE in code units, AFTER in bytes. Vectors: corpus/rules/sync.json, `keys-of-digits-sort-as-text`, `keys-that-look-like-numbers-stay-text`, `keys-sort-by-utf16-unit`.

x-markers.description: The three markers the format 2 adds to the text of a line. Grammar only: what they mean is `x-writer-guarantees` and the reading rules. N is a canonical decimal of at most nine digits (no sign, no leading zero). A list name holds none of ] [ : = *. The C# (LineMarkers) is held to these patterns by the checks; the site and the editors port them as written.

x-writer-guarantees.description: What a writer owes a file before a line is written (LineWrites.Refusal, draft §6). Checked at the door (`upload`) and by every editor, in this order, the first failing one being the reason given. Everything but `format-2-field-in-format-1` applies to a file of the format 2 only: in a format 1 file a `[!g*0]` is the game's text.

codes.format-2-field-in-format-1: a line holds a field of the format 2 and the file says it is format 1 (`_engine_version` absent, 0 or 1)
codes.carriage-return-in-text: a text of the format 2 (a form, a link's `was` or `to`, a refused entry) holds a carriage return: they are LF only, like `v` and the keys — no side normalises them before hashing
codes.marker-without-link: the text shows `[!g*N]` and the line holds no `links[N]`
codes.link-without-marker: the line holds `links[N]` and its text has no `[!g*N]`
codes.link-entry-missing: a link's `to` is not the key of a line of this file
codes.link-form-missing: a link names a form its entry's `forms` does not hold (`0` is always the entry's own `v`)
codes.token-invalid: a game token (`_lists.tokens`) is empty, holds a carriage return, or holds a marker `[!`
codes.tokens-not-in-order: the game tokens are not in the strictly ascending ordinal order (UTF-16 code units): unsorted, or one twice
codes.slot-list-missing: a slot of the key or of `v` names a list `_lists` does not hold, or agrees with something that is neither such a list nor an open slot of the key
codes.slot-open-missing: `v` shows `[!T*N]` and the key has no `[!T*N]`
codes.use-form-missing: a `use` of the line names a form the line does not hold
codes.entry-has-link-marker: a term, or the entry a link points at, shows a `[!g*N]` in its own text or in one of its forms: a term does not cite another term
codes.template-id-collision: two different templates of the file have the same derived id (file-level: TemplateIds.Collision)
codes.machine-changed-person-line: the machine writes: it changed the `v`, `forms` or `class` of a line a person wrote or validated (tag H or V)
codes.machine-wrote-person-link: the machine writes: a link with `by: "H"` the line did not already hold
codes.machine-wrote-unlinked: the machine writes: `unlinked` the line did not already hold

propertyNames.$comment: LF only: a key holding CR is not the written form. Every reader normalises CRLF, so a Core that writes it has keys the site never finds.

if.$comment: The file says it is format 1 (`_engine_version` absent, 0 or 1).

then.$comment: ...so no line holds a field of the format 2. The names above are the metadata, spared from the line form (the same list as `properties` and `not.propertyNames.enum`).

not.$comment: At least one line: a file made only of metadata has nothing to publish and is refused at the door.

uuid.description: A lowercase GUID. The site's door is wider ([A-Za-z0-9-]{1,36}) for files written before this was fixed; a Core writes a GUID.

hash.description: SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex digits, no prefix.

language.description: A language name exactly as catalogs/languages.json spells it (the name IS the upload contract).

line.description: One line: the key is the game's text, the value what to show instead.

v.description: The translation, LF only. Empty or null = a capture waiting for one (with t = H), or a line the model declined (with t = S, where v then repeats the key).

t.description: Who wrote it: H a human, V a human validated a machine's, A a machine, S skipped (not in the source language; v = the key), M the mod's own interface — legacy in this file, interface lines live in modui-translate.json and a reader takes them out.

i.description: Capture order, for the web editors to sort by. Omitted when absent, never null. Presentation only: excluded from every hash and every merge comparison.

lineV2.description: A line of a file of the format 2: the format 1 line, and the fields below, each written only when it holds something. A file that says it is format 1 may hold none of them (the `then` of the root). The content hash writes them after v and t in the order listed here (common Sync.cs, ContentHash).

term.description: « This text names a thing of the game », set by a person or the machine, even before any sentence points at it. Absent, never false. An entry of a list the game holds is one without it.

forms.description: The written forms of this entry (LF only, like every text) (« pièces d'étoile », « de la pièce d'étoile »), by form id. An id is given once and never reused — it does not depend on a template or on an extraction pass. `0` is the entry's own `v`, never listed. Meant to be few: a form is kept once, and a template or a sentence points at it.

use.description: What each template takes from this entry, by template id: one form id, or one per agreement class (`[!L*a=b]`). An entry with no `use` for a template gives its own `v`.

class.description: The agreement class this entry gives in each template it governs, by template id.

oracle.description: On a template's line: how it was made — `accepted` as it stands, `refused` and assembled anyway (to be read again), `line` taken from a line, `repeated-name` a name the game draws from repeated entries.

links.description: The links of the sentence. The position is the N of the `[!g*N]` of `v`: no hole, no marker without one, no link without a marker (`x-writer-guarantees`).

unlinked.description: Entries a PERSON said this sentence does not name (« here, this word is not that term »). The machine never writes one; a person's refusal outlasts every later extraction.

link.description: « Here is written such an entry, in such a form ». Reading it (common LinkReading): the form asked of the entry, with its case; the form gone → the entry's translation; the entry gone → `was`; never a hole, never the marker. « To read again » is computed: what the link reads today is no longer `was`.

to.description: The KEY of the entry's line (a line's key is unique: no list is named).

form.description: The form asked of the entry. Absent = the entry's own translation.

case.description: How the sentence writes the case of that text: the first letter as a capital, or as a small letter (measured: only the first letter differs, and never at the head of a sentence). Absent = as the form is written. Applying it is the reader's own Unicode data, never the machine's culture.

by.description: A the machine set it, H a person set or confirmed it.

was.description: The text read when the link was set or confirmed — as the sentence shows it, case included. Saving or validating the sentence puts it back.

own.description: The writing of THIS sentence alone, when a person wrote the term otherwise here and kept the link (`Only this text`). It passes before every form, never follows the term, and is never to read again. LF only.

formId.description: A form id of an entry: `f` and a positive decimal, given once and never reused. It starts with a letter on purpose: an integer-looking key is turned into a number by PHP arrays (numeric sort, re-encoded as a list). Sorted as TEXT by the hash (f1, f10, f2).

formRef.description: A form id, or `0` for the entry's own `v` (a value, never a key).

name.description: An agreement class name: starts with a letter on purpose (see formId).

templateId.description: The id of a template, DERIVED from its key: `t` and the first 12 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the key in UTF-8, line breaks LF (common TemplateIds.Of, corpus rules/template_ids.json). Never stored on the template, so two writers cannot disagree; two templates of one file with the same id are refused.
